content: Kinectin is a protein in humans that is encoded by the KTN1 gene. Various cellular organelles and vesicles are transported along microtubules within the cytoplasm. Similarly, processes such as the recycling of membranes in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER), the assembly of the Golgi apparatus at the microtubule organizing center, and the alignment of lysosomes along microtubules are all related to this transport system. The transport of organelles depends on a specific class of microtubule-associated proteins (MAPs). One of these proteins is the molecular motor kinesin, which is an ATPase that facilitates the unidirectional movement of vesicles toward the plus end of the microtubule (refer to MIM 148760 and MIM 600025 for more details). Another MAP involved in this process is kinectin, which is a large integral membrane protein of the ER. Antibodies targeting kinectin have been demonstrated to inhibit its ability to bind to kinesin. The KTN1 protein has been shown to interact with EEF1D, RhoG, and RHOA.
